subject.title: Guard Telegram and iMessage dispatch against fleet loops

question: Should Telegram/iMessage loop suppression be accepted as a shared provider-dispatcher subprocess guard, or must it be implemented as an OpenClaw-owned channel/SDK guard before session recording?
rationale: The PR introduces a new executable trust boundary and owner-boundary change on message dispatch; repository policy and current code point toward channel-owned in-process loop protection, but accepting a subprocess guard would require explicit maintainer security and operations intent.

options.title: Require in-process channel guard
options.body: Move suppression into channel-owned or shared channel-turn loop protection before session recording, and remove the external binary/env dependency.

options.title: Accept external guard intentionally
options.body: Allow the subprocess design only with documented install ownership, security review, real transport proof, and upgrade/operator guidance.

options.title: Pause in favor of narrower work
options.body: Keep this PR unmerged while Telegram-specific bot policy and iMessage-specific loop prevention are handled through narrower channel PRs.

recommendation.title: Require in-process channel guard
recommendation.body: Move suppression into channel-owned or shared channel-turn loop protection before session recording, and remove the external binary/env dependency.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history points to this person across the central dispatcher and channel-turn files that define the owner boundary.
